subject: Throughput stability amendment request — Synergiya reserved GPUs
messages:
From: Jared Park <jared.park@synergiya.io>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: megan.torres@synergiya.io
Date: 2026-10-18 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request — reserved GPU throughput stability for nightly ETL spikes

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We rolled Redwood Dedicated into production last month and overall things look great. One friction point: our nightly ETL + synthetic inference window (00:00–03:00 local) causes bursty throughput that collides with co-tenant batch jobs and we see queueing delays that affect SLAs for our downstream pipelines.

Our legal and SRE teams asked whether we can get an amendment to the reserved GPU terms to guarantee a minimum sustained throughput (tokens/sec) during our scheduled night window, or alternatively a predictable "night-burst" allocation. We're not asking to block other tenants entirely — just a carveout or guaranteed headroom for 2.5 hours daily, and clear crediting if we fall below the bound.

I've attached a short request doc and some numbers (Synergiya_SLA_Request.pdf, synergiya_headroom_estimates.xlsx). High-level asks:
- Guaranteed sustained throughput floor: ~120k tokens/min across our reserved pool between 00:00–02:30 PT.
- Queueing behavior: no preemptions for inflight requests under 3s token latency unless higher-priority incidents are declared.
- Clear fallback: if capacity is constrained, Redwood routes requests to a compatible warm variant with documented latency delta and credits us for the delta.

Can we set up a call with your SRE and legal to discuss feasibility and commercial impact?

Best,
Jared
Head of Platform Engineering
Synergiya, Inc.

-- Attachment stubs:
- Synergiya_SLA_Request.pdf (pdf)
- synergiya_headroom_estimates.xlsx (xlsx)

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: Jared Park <jared.park@synergiya.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — reserved GPU throughput stability for nightly ETL spikes

Jared — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. I can see why this is a blocker for the pipeline SLA.

High level options we should evaluate quickly:
1) Night-burst carveout: reserve an explicit nightly headroom slice (e.g., 2 GPUs equivalent for the 00:00–02:30 PT window) with a small uplift to the monthly commit.
2) Priority-lane SLO: keep your current pool but run a soft-priority lane for identified routes — preemptible under severer service incidents but otherwise insulated from co-tenant batch eviction.
3) Fallback routing + crediting: allow automatic fallback to a slightly larger quantized model variant. If fallback increases P95 latency beyond your target, we credit token cost difference and issue throughput credits.

Action items I propose:
- Ben, can you calculate commercial impact for options (1) and (2) (sheet + delta)?
- Laura, can you coordinate a quick SRE review to estimate implementation and monitoring overhead for the fallback-credit flow (we'd need trace hooks and an audit metric)?
- Jared/ Megan — can you confirm the exact timezone for the window (is it PT?) and whether the 120k tokens/min is a sustained or peak requirement?

I can host a 30-min sync tomorrow if that works — propose 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Principal Account Lead
Redwood Inference

-- Attachment referenced: draft_amendment_v1.docx (docx)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, Jared Park <jared.park@synergiya.io>

Date: 2026-10-18 20:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — reserved GPU throughput stability for nightly ETL spikes

All — ran quick numbers against Synergiya's sheet. Two quick sketches: 
A) Night-burst carveout (2-GPU equivalent for 2.5 hours daily): ~+14% to monthly reserved commit (ballpark), one-time amendment fee if we need guaranteed isolation.
B) Priority-lane SLO (no new reserved commit): small monthly fee + monitoring surcharge. We'd cap daily total burst tokens and convert excess to post-paid usage.

I uploaded a short commercial spreadsheet and a draft amendment outline here: https://drive.redwood.example/synergiya/sla-request (see tab "Commercial_Sketch").

If Synergiya really needs deterministic in-flight protection (no preemptions under 3s token latency), that's closer to option A + legal acceptance of an isolation SLA; that'll require SRE runbook changes and an ops addendum. Laura — want to sync on engineering cost baseline tomorrow at 9:15 PT?

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, Jared Park <jared.park@synergiya.io>
Date: 2026-10-19 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — Request — reserved GPU throughput stability for nightly ETL spikes

Jared / team — quick SRE readout below after 1-hour triage: 
- Implementation complexity: low-medium. We already have tenant priority lanes and nightly maintenance windows; the main work is adding per-tenant scheduled headroom and a crediting metric if rounding falls short.
- Monitoring/observability: we need a per-tenant P95 token-latency SLI and a "headroom shortfall" counter. That requires an instrumentation change + 72-hr test window to validate accuracy.
- Risk: medium for noisy neighbors during platform-wide peak (e.g., large model rollouts). We can mitigate via staged rollout and explicit blackout windows for platform ops.

Suggested technical proposal for legal: 
1) Define nightly "headroom allocation" (GPU-equivalent) and a guaranteed sustained throughput floor (tokens/min) during the window.
2) If shortfall occurs, Redwood credits the account proportional to minutes of shortfall * baseline token-cost multiplier (formula in draft).
3) Allow preemption only during declared platform severity incidents; otherwise preemption limited for inflight requests with token-latency < 3s.

I'll attach an SRE impact note to the draft amendment and share the instrumentation checklist. We should be explicit about test windows and an initial 60-day probation period.

Laura Bennett
Head, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Jared Park <jared.park@synergiya.io>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — reserved GPU throughput stability for nightly ETL spikes

Evelyn/Ben/Laura — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the proposed options. Confirming: window is PT and 120k tokens/min is a sustained average target for the 00:00–02:30 window. We're happy to do a 60-day probation and run the instrumentation test window.

We prefer option A (night-burst carveout) if the uplift is reasonable — we can sign an amendment quickly if SRE and Legal provide the doc. 10:00 PT tomorrow for the sync works for us.

-Jared
